**Observations:**

- **Affected part**: Underside of a tomato leaf (leaf is curled/rolled showing the ventral surface prominently)
- **Key visual features**:
  - Dense, white to grayish-white powdery/fluffy coating covering most of the leaf underside
  - Coating is uniform and thick — not discrete spots but a broad confluent layer
  - Leaf venation still visible through the white growth
  - Healthy green tissue visible at leaf margins and on adjacent leaves
  - No visible brown/tan lesions, concentric rings, or water-soaked areas

**Differential reasoning:**

| Disease | Fit |
|---|---|
| **Powdery_Mildew** | Excellent — "dense white layer of growth on both surfaces," "white powdery sporulation on undersides," leaves wither but remain attached |
| Late_Blight | Poor — requires purple-brown blotches first; cottony sporulation is thinner and patchy |
| Leaf_Mold | Poor — color would be olive-green to brown, not white |
| Gray_Mold | Poor — gray mold typically follows tissue necrosis/rot |

The dense, uniform, bright-white powdery coating across the entire leaf underside, with no associated brown lesions or necrotic spots, is the hallmark presentation of **Powdery Mildew**.
